question: Which of the following is NOT the primary goal of Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme?

options.text: To increase the government regulation in the private operation significantly.

solution:
The correct answer is __**To increase the government regulation in the private operation significantly.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme** is designed to promote manufacturing in India by offering incentives to firms based on their production output.
 
• The primary goals of the PLI scheme include attracting substantial investments, incorporating advanced technology, and improving operational efficiency. These objectives aim to enhance India's manufacturing capabilities and global competitiveness.
 
• The scheme seeks to reduce import dependency by encouraging domestic production and fostering a self-reliant economy, in line with the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
• However, the scheme does not aim to significantly increase government regulation in the private sector. Instead, it focuses on providing support and incentives to industries to boost their output and encourage ease of doing business.
 
• The correct answer is related to the fact that the PLI scheme is designed to **empower industries** rather than impose excessive regulatory burdens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overview of the PLI Scheme:**

 
 
• The scheme was launched in **2020** by the Government of India to boost domestic manufacturing and enhance export capabilities.
 
• It focuses on sectors such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, textiles, and more, with incentives linked to incremental production.
 
• The scheme is expected to generate large-scale employment and make India a global manufacturing hub.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the PLI Scheme:**
 
 
• **Attract substantial investments:** The scheme encourages both domestic and foreign investors to set up manufacturing units in India.
 
• **Incorporate advanced technology:** It aims to modernize the manufacturing process by adopting cutting-edge technologies.
 
• **Ensure operational efficiency:** By improving productivity and reducing inefficiencies, the scheme seeks to make Indian products globally competitive.
 
 
 
• **Important Sectors under the Scheme:**
 
 
• **Electronics:** The PLI scheme supports local production of mobile phones, semiconductors, and other electronic components.
 
• **Automobiles:** Incentives are provided for advanced automotive technology and electric vehicles.
 
• **Pharmaceuticals:** The scheme promotes the production of key starting materials (KSMs) and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).
 
• **Textiles:** It aims to boost the production of man-made fibers and technical textiles.
 
 
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• The incentives are performance-based, with financial benefits provided for achieving incremental output targets.
 
• It is implemented in a phased manner, with different sectors being added over time.
 
• The scheme complements other government initiatives like **Make in India** and **Digital India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Budget Allocation:** The total outlay for the PLI scheme across various sectors is approximately **₹1.97 lakh crore** over a five-year period.
 
• **Success Metrics:** The scheme is expected to add **$500 billion** to India's manufacturing output annually and create millions of jobs.
 
• **Key Beneficiaries:** Large multinational corporations and domestic manufacturers with the capability to scale up production are the primary beneficiaries.
 
• **Global Comparison:** Similar schemes have been implemented in countries like **China**, which used production incentives to establish itself as a manufacturing powerhouse.
